name: netdryrun-network-change-verdict-corpus
how_to_use: For each case, copy the base lab, apply the case's edits (replace the text in the named node's config, or append a line), then decide whether the change is safe. 'expected' is the label.
how_labels_were_decided: Written before any run, by one maintainer's judgment: would an experienced operator reject this change in review because it causes harm? Not derived from the checks. Labels are the maintainer's, not independent ground truth.

edit_format.replace/with: exact text to find and its replacement
edit_format.append: a line added at the end of the config

amendments: corpus/AMENDMENTS.md and corpus/v2/AMENDMENTS.md list every label or case change made after a run.

base.topology.clab.yml:
# Verdict Corpus base network: a small provider (AS65000, routers pe1 + pe2) with one
# customer (ce1), one upstream transit (up1) and one settlement-free peer (peer1).
#
#   ce1 (AS65100) --- pe1 ===iBGP=== pe2 --- peer1 (AS65300)
#                      |
#                     up1 (AS65200, transit, sends a default)
#
# Policy intent (see ../INTENT.md): customers' routes go everywhere; routes learned from
# the upstream or the peer go to customers only (no free transit, i.e. no route leaks).
name: ndr-corpus

topology:
  defaults:
    kind: linux
    image: quay.io/frrouting/frr:10.4.1
  nodes:
    ce1:
      binds: [configs/daemons:/etc/frr/daemons, configs/vtysh.conf:/etc/frr/vtysh.conf, configs/ce1.conf:/etc/frr/frr.conf]
    pe1:
      binds: [configs/daemons:/etc/frr/daemons, configs/vtysh.conf:/etc/frr/vtysh.conf, configs/pe1.conf:/etc/frr/frr.conf]
    pe2:
      binds: [configs/daemons:/etc/frr/daemons, configs/vtysh.conf:/etc/frr/vtysh.conf, configs/pe2.conf:/etc/frr/frr.conf]
    up1:
      binds: [configs/daemons:/etc/frr/daemons, configs/vtysh.conf:/etc/frr/vtysh.conf, configs/up1.conf:/etc/frr/frr.conf]
    peer1:
      binds: [configs/daemons:/etc/frr/daemons, configs/vtysh.conf:/etc/frr/vtysh.conf, configs/peer1.conf:/etc/frr/frr.conf]
  links:
    - endpoints: ["ce1:eth1", "pe1:eth1"]     # 10.0.1.0/30
    - endpoints: ["pe1:eth2", "up1:eth1"]     # 10.0.2.0/30
    - endpoints: ["pe1:eth3", "pe2:eth1"]     # 10.0.3.0/30
    - endpoints: ["pe2:eth2", "peer1:eth1"]   # 10.0.4.0/30
base.configs/ce1.conf:
frr defaults traditional
hostname ce1
!
interface lo
 ip address 10.100.0.1/24
!
interface eth1
 ip address 10.0.1.2/30
!
route-map ALLOW-ALL permit 10
!
router bgp 65100
 bgp router-id 10.100.0.1
 neighbor 10.0.1.1 remote-as 65000
 address-family ipv4 unicast
  network 10.100.0.0/24
  neighbor 10.0.1.1 route-map ALLOW-ALL in
  neighbor 10.0.1.1 route-map ALLOW-ALL out
 exit-address-family
!
base.configs/daemons:
zebra=yes
bgpd=yes
ospfd=no
ospf6d=no
ripd=no
ripngd=no
isisd=no
pimd=no
ldpd=no
nhrpd=no
eigrpd=no
babeld=no
sharpd=no
staticd=yes
pbrd=no
bfdd=no
fabricd=no
vrrpd=no

vtysh_enable=yes
zebra_options="  -A 127.0.0.1 -s 90000000"
bgpd_options="   -A 127.0.0.1"
staticd_options="-A 127.0.0.1"
base.configs/pe1.conf:
frr defaults traditional
hostname pe1
!
interface lo
 ip address 10.255.0.1/32
!
interface eth1
 description to-customer-ce1
 ip address 10.0.1.1/30
!
interface eth2
 description to-upstream-up1
 ip address 10.0.2.1/30
!
interface eth3
 description to-pe2
 ip address 10.0.3.1/30
!
! Our own aggregate, originated from a discard route
ip route 192.0.2.0/24 blackhole
!
ip prefix-list OWN seq 10 permit 192.0.2.0/24
ip prefix-list CUSTOMER-IN seq 10 permit 10.100.0.0/22 le 24
!
bgp community-list standard CUSTOMER permit 65000:100
!
route-map FROM-CUSTOMER permit 10
 match ip address prefix-list CUSTOMER-IN
 set community 65000:100
 set local-preference 300
!
route-map FROM-UPSTREAM permit 10
 set community 65000:200
 set local-preference 100
!
route-map TO-UPSTREAM permit 10
 match community CUSTOMER
!
route-map TO-UPSTREAM permit 20
 match ip address prefix-list OWN
!
route-map TO-CUSTOMER permit 10
!
router bgp 65000
 bgp router-id 10.255.0.1
 neighbor 10.0.1.2 remote-as 65100
 neighbor 10.0.1.2 description ce1
 neighbor 10.0.2.2 remote-as 65200
 neighbor 10.0.2.2 description up1
 neighbor 10.0.3.2 remote-as 65000
 neighbor 10.0.3.2 description pe2
 address-family ipv4 unicast
  network 192.0.2.0/24
  neighbor 10.0.1.2 route-map FROM-CUSTOMER in
  neighbor 10.0.1.2 route-map TO-CUSTOMER out
  neighbor 10.0.1.2 maximum-prefix 100
  neighbor 10.0.2.2 route-map FROM-UPSTREAM in
  neighbor 10.0.2.2 route-map TO-UPSTREAM out
  neighbor 10.0.3.2 next-hop-self
  neighbor 10.0.3.2 send-community
 exit-address-family
!
base.configs/pe2.conf:
frr defaults traditional
hostname pe2
!
interface lo
 ip address 10.255.0.2/32
!
interface eth1
 description to-pe1
 ip address 10.0.3.2/30
!
interface eth2
 description to-peer-peer1
 ip address 10.0.4.1/30
!
ip prefix-list OWN seq 10 permit 192.0.2.0/24
ip prefix-list PEER-IN seq 10 permit 198.51.100.0/24
!
bgp community-list standard CUSTOMER permit 65000:100
!
route-map FROM-PEER permit 10
 match ip address prefix-list PEER-IN
 set community 65000:300
 set local-preference 200
!
route-map TO-PEER permit 10
 match community CUSTOMER
!
route-map TO-PEER permit 20
 match ip address prefix-list OWN
!
router bgp 65000
 bgp router-id 10.255.0.2
 neighbor 10.0.3.1 remote-as 65000
 neighbor 10.0.3.1 description pe1
 neighbor 10.0.4.2 remote-as 65300
 neighbor 10.0.4.2 description peer1
 address-family ipv4 unicast
  neighbor 10.0.3.1 next-hop-self
  neighbor 10.0.3.1 send-community
  neighbor 10.0.4.2 route-map FROM-PEER in
  neighbor 10.0.4.2 route-map TO-PEER out
 exit-address-family
!
base.configs/peer1.conf:
frr defaults traditional
hostname peer1
!
interface lo
 ip address 198.51.100.1/24
!
interface eth1
 ip address 10.0.4.2/30
!
route-map ALLOW-ALL permit 10
!
router bgp 65300
 bgp router-id 198.51.100.1
 neighbor 10.0.4.1 remote-as 65000
 address-family ipv4 unicast
  network 198.51.100.0/24
  neighbor 10.0.4.1 route-map ALLOW-ALL in
  neighbor 10.0.4.1 route-map ALLOW-ALL out
 exit-address-family
!
base.configs/up1.conf:
frr defaults traditional
hostname up1
!
interface lo
 ip address 203.0.113.1/24
!
interface eth1
 ip address 10.0.2.2/30
!
route-map ALLOW-ALL permit 10
!
router bgp 65200
 bgp router-id 203.0.113.1
 neighbor 10.0.2.1 remote-as 65000
 address-family ipv4 unicast
  network 203.0.113.0/24
  neighbor 10.0.2.1 default-originate
  neighbor 10.0.2.1 route-map ALLOW-ALL in
  neighbor 10.0.2.1 route-map ALLOW-ALL out
 exit-address-family
!

cases.title: No change (control)
cases.rationale: The base network with no edits. Every strategy must pass it, or the corpus itself is broken.

cases.title: Set MED on routes sent to the upstream
cases.rationale: Adds a metric to the upstream export clause. Changes path attributes only; nothing leaks or disappears.

edits.append:
route-map TO-UPSTREAM permit 10
 set metric 50

cases.title: Prepend our AS twice toward the peer
cases.rationale: Routine inbound traffic engineering. The same prefixes are still announced.

edits.append:
route-map TO-PEER permit 10
 set as-path prepend 65000 65000

cases.title: Tag our aggregate with an informational community toward the upstream
cases.rationale: Adds a community on the OWN clause. Attribute change only.

edits.append:
route-map TO-UPSTREAM permit 20
 set community 65000:999 additive

cases.title: Change an interface description
cases.rationale: Cosmetic change. Must never be blocked.

cases.title: Customer announces a second allowed /24
cases.rationale: The customer adds 10.100.1.0/24, inside its registered 10.100.0.0/22. Announcing it upstream is the desired outcome.
cases.note: Normal customer growth inside the registered range.

edits.append:
ip route 10.100.1.0/24 blackhole
router bgp 65100
 address-family ipv4 unicast
  network 10.100.1.0/24
 exit-address-family

cases.title: Lower the customer maximum-prefix from 100 to 50
cases.rationale: Tightening a safety limit that is still far above the customer's real count.

cases.title: Shorten BGP timers toward the upstream
cases.rationale: Faster failure detection; the session stays up.

edits.append:
router bgp 65000
 neighbor 10.0.2.2 timers 10 30

cases.title: Lower customer local-preference from 300 to 250
cases.rationale: Customer routes stay the most preferred (peer 200, upstream 100).

cases.title: Upstream export filter replaced with permit-all
cases.rationale: pe1 now announces everything to the upstream, including the peer's route: free transit for the peer, a classic route leak.
cases.note: Route leak as defined in RFC 7908.

cases.title: Peer export filter replaced with permit-all
cases.rationale: pe2 announces upstream routes and the default to the peer: a route leak toward the peer.
cases.note: Route leak as defined in RFC 7908.

edits.append: route-map ALLOW-ALL permit 10

cases.title: send-community removed on the pe1 to pe2 iBGP session
cases.rationale: pe2 no longer sees the customer community, so it stops announcing the customer route to the peer.
cases.note: A common mistake when rebuilding iBGP sessions.

cases.title: Typo in the upstream's ASN (65020 instead of 65200)
cases.rationale: The upstream session never comes up; the customer loses internet access.

cases.title: Peer session administratively shut down
cases.rationale: The peer route disappears and the peer loses our routes.

edits.append:
router bgp 65000
 neighbor 10.0.4.2 shutdown

cases.title: Customer prefix-list typo rejects the customer's /24
cases.rationale: le 23 instead of le 24 drops the customer's only prefix, so the customer becomes unreachable from the internet.

cases.title: Upstream export policy denies everything
cases.rationale: Every route we announce to the upstream is withdrawn: our aggregate and the customer vanish from the upstream.
cases.note: Mass-withdrawal outage class (the 2021 Facebook outage began with withdrawn routes).

edits.replace:
route-map TO-UPSTREAM permit 10
 match community CUSTOMER
!
route-map TO-UPSTREAM permit 20
 match ip address prefix-list OWN

cases.title: default-originate configured toward the peer
cases.rationale: We offer the peer a default route, so the peer can send all its traffic through us for free.

edits.append:
router bgp 65000
 address-family ipv4 unicast
  neighbor 10.0.4.2 default-originate
 exit-address-family

cases.title: redistribute connected added on pe1
cases.rationale: Infrastructure /30s and loopbacks go to the customer and into iBGP. Export filters keep them from the upstream and the peer, but leaking infrastructure to customers is rejected in review.
cases.note: Not covered by the intent spec, which has no check for infrastructure routes at the customer.

edits.append:
router bgp 65000
 address-family ipv4 unicast
  redistribute connected
 exit-address-family

cases.title: next-hop-self removed on pe2 toward pe1
cases.rationale: pe1 learns the peer route with an unreachable next hop, so the customer loses the peer route.

cases.title: iBGP session between pe1 and pe2 shut down
cases.rationale: The two halves of the network stop exchanging routes.

edits.append:
router bgp 65000
 neighbor 10.0.3.2 shutdown

cases.title: Customer maximum-prefix safety limit removed
cases.rationale: Nothing changes today, but a customer leaking a full table would now be accepted. Reviewers reject removing safety limits.
cases.note: Latent risk: no steady-state check can see it until the customer actually leaks. Catching it needs a failure-injection scenario (the customer sends many prefixes), planned for a later release.

cases.title: Customer announces someone else's prefix; our filter blocks it
cases.rationale: ce1 starts announcing 8.8.8.0/24. pe1's customer filter rejects it, so nothing leaks. The customer-side change is bad, but our network behaves correctly, so a test of our network must pass.

edits.append:
ip route 8.8.8.0/24 blackhole
router bgp 65100
 address-family ipv4 unicast
  network 8.8.8.0/24
 exit-address-family

cases.title: pe1 accidentally originates 8.8.8.0/24
cases.rationale: A fat-fingered network statement hijacks 8.8.8.0/24 for our own customer. Export filters keep it from the upstream and the peer.
cases.note: Not covered by the intent spec, which has no check for unexpected routes at the customer.

edits.append:
ip route 8.8.8.0/24 blackhole
router bgp 65000
 address-family ipv4 unicast
  network 8.8.8.0/24
 exit-address-family

cases.title: Static discard route for the customer prefix on pe1
cases.rationale: The static route beats BGP, so traffic to the customer is dropped while the route is still announced.

edits.with:
ip route 192.0.2.0/24 blackhole
ip route 10.100.0.0/24 blackhole

cases.title: Aggregate network statement typo (192.0.3.0/24)
cases.rationale: Our own aggregate is no longer announced anywhere.

cases.title: A permit-everything clause inserted before the peer export filter
cases.rationale: Sequence 5 matches everything, so upstream routes and the default leak to the peer.

edits.append: route-map TO-PEER permit 5

cases.title: pe2 configured with the wrong local ASN
cases.rationale: All of pe2's sessions fail and the peer is cut off.

cases.title: Customer inbound route-map removed
cases.rationale: Without the import policy the customer's routes lose their community (or are rejected outright), so they are no longer exported upstream.

cases.title: Enable BGP graceful restart on pe1
cases.rationale: A resilience feature; the routing outcome is unchanged.

edits.append:
router bgp 65000
 bgp graceful-restart

cases.title: Peer inbound filter replaced with permit-all
cases.rationale: Nothing changes today because the peer only sends its /24, but the peer could now send a default or bogons. Reviewers reject removing an import filter.
cases.note: Latent risk: invisible in steady state until the peer misbehaves. Needs a failure-injection scenario.

edits.append: route-map ALLOW-ALL permit 10

cases.title: No change (control)
cases.rationale: The base lab runs unchanged. Every strategy must call it safe, including while the two misbehaving-neighbor scenarios run.

cases.title: redistribute connected added on pe2
cases.rationale: pe2's link /30s, its loopback and the management subnet become BGP routes. The peer export filter keeps them from the peer, but they reach pe1 over iBGP and go on to the customer. Reviewers reject leaking infrastructure to customers. (Re-expresses v1 case 18 on the other router.)

edits.append:
router bgp 65000
 address-family ipv4 unicast
  redistribute connected
 exit-address-family

cases.title: pe1 originates 1.1.1.0/24 left over from a lab test
cases.rationale: A network statement for 1.1.1.0/24 (often used as junk space in tests) is left in the production config. Our customer's traffic to the public resolver at 1.1.1.1 is now blackholed by us. Export filters keep it from the upstream and the peer. (Re-expresses v1 case 23 with a prefix on the I7 sentinel list.)

edits.append:
ip route 1.1.1.0/24 blackhole
router bgp 65000
 address-family ipv4 unicast
  network 1.1.1.0/24
 exit-address-family

cases.title: Aggregate added on pe2 for redundancy, mistyped as 192.0.12.0/24
cases.rationale: The operator meant to originate our 192.0.2.0/24 from pe2 too, but typed 192.0.12.0/24, someone else's space. The peer export filter only allows our real aggregate, so the peer does not see it, but pe1 sends it to the customer, whose traffic to that network is now blackholed. (v1 case 23 class with a prefix that is not on any sentinel list.)
cases.note: Expected to be missed. I7 only spot-checks a few well-known prefixes, and nothing bounds what the customer receives.

edits.append:
ip route 192.0.12.0/24 blackhole
router bgp 65000
 address-family ipv4 unicast
  network 192.0.12.0/24
 exit-address-family

cases.title: Customer maximum-prefix safety limit removed
cases.rationale: Nothing changes in steady state, but a customer that floods us with more-specifics from its /16 would now have all of them accepted and passed to the upstream and the peer. Reviewers reject removing safety limits. (Re-expresses v1 case 21, now with a limit that can trip.)

cases.title: Peer inbound filter replaced with permit-all
cases.rationale: Nothing changes today because the peer only sends its /24, but anything the peer sends is now accepted, including a more-specific of our customer's space that would hijack the customer's traffic. Reviewers reject removing an import filter. (Re-expresses v1 case 30.)

edits.append: route-map ALLOW-ALL permit 10

cases.title: Customer announces two more /24s from its /16
cases.rationale: The customer adds 10.100.1.0/24 and 10.100.2.0/24, inside its registered 10.100.0.0/16. Announcing them upstream and to the peer is the desired outcome. (Re-expresses v1 case 06, which v1's exact prefix count wrongly blocked.)

edits.append:
ip route 10.100.1.0/24 blackhole
ip route 10.100.2.0/24 blackhole
router bgp 65100
 address-family ipv4 unicast
  network 10.100.1.0/24
  network 10.100.2.0/24
 exit-address-family

cases.title: Customer also announces its covering /16
cases.rationale: The customer starts announcing 10.100.0.0/16, its registered block, alongside the /24. The import filter allows it (le 24 includes the /16 itself), and a customer announcing its own allocation is normal.

edits.append:
ip route 10.100.0.0/16 blackhole
router bgp 65100
 address-family ipv4 unicast
  network 10.100.0.0/16
 exit-address-family

cases.title: Explicit send-community line removed on the pe1 to pe2 iBGP session
cases.rationale: FRR sends communities to every neighbor by default, so deleting the explicit line is a no-op and pe2 still sees the customer community. Labeled from v1's measured post-run finding on case 12, not from fresh judgment (see INTENT.md). On platforms that do not send communities by default, the same edit would be harmful.

cases.title: Standard communities explicitly disabled on the pe1 to pe2 iBGP session
cases.rationale: pe1 stops sending standard communities to pe2, so the customer route arrives at pe2 without 65000:100. pe2's peer export policy matches on that community, so the customer route stops reaching the peer: the customer loses the peering path it pays for.

cases.title: Customer maximum-prefix changed to warning-only
cases.rationale: The limit now only logs a warning instead of shutting the session, so a customer flood is accepted and passed on. A common "temporary" change after a limit tripped once. Nothing changes in steady state.

cases.title: Customer maximum-prefix raised from 50 to 100
cases.rationale: The customer is growing and asked for a higher limit. The limit still exists and still shuts the session on a flood well beyond the customer's needs.

cases.title: Upstream import policy tags routes with the customer community (copy-paste error)
cases.rationale: FROM-UPSTREAM now sets 65000:100 instead of 65000:200. Every export policy treats upstream routes as customer routes, so the upstream's routes and its default are announced to the peer, giving the peer free transit through our upstream.

cases.title: Customer export policy restricted to the default route
cases.rationale: A default-only template is applied to a customer that pays for full routes. The customer still has connectivity through the default but loses the specific routes it needs for its own traffic engineering, which breaks its contract.

edits.append: ip prefix-list DEFAULT-ONLY seq 10 permit 0.0.0.0/0

edits.with:
route-map TO-CUSTOMER permit 10
 match ip address prefix-list DEFAULT-ONLY

cases.title: Default route from the upstream filtered on import
cases.rationale: A deny clause for 0.0.0.0/0 is added to FROM-UPSTREAM ("we don't need a default from transit"). In this network the upstream's default is how the customer reaches everything beyond the two lab prefixes, so the customer loses most of the internet.

edits.append:
ip prefix-list DEFAULT-ONLY seq 10 permit 0.0.0.0/0
route-map FROM-UPSTREAM deny 5
 match ip address prefix-list DEFAULT-ONLY

cases.title: Customer session moved into a CUSTOMERS peer-group
cases.rationale: A refactor that moves the customer's route-maps and limit onto a peer-group so future customers share them. The customer's effective policy is unchanged.

edits.with:
neighbor CUSTOMERS peer-group
 neighbor 10.0.1.2 remote-as 65100
 neighbor 10.0.1.2 peer-group CUSTOMERS

edits.replace:
neighbor 10.0.1.2 route-map FROM-CUSTOMER in
  neighbor 10.0.1.2 route-map TO-CUSTOMER out
  neighbor 10.0.1.2 maximum-prefix 50 restart 1
edits.with:
neighbor CUSTOMERS route-map FROM-CUSTOMER in
  neighbor CUSTOMERS route-map TO-CUSTOMER out
  neighbor CUSTOMERS maximum-prefix 50 restart 1

cases.title: Add an informational region community to customer routes
cases.rationale: Customer routes get 65000:110 (region tag) next to 65000:100. The export policies match on 65000:100, which is still present, so nothing else changes.

cases.title: Discard route for our aggregate deleted as unused
cases.rationale: The blackhole static for 192.0.2.0/24 looks unused and is cleaned up. Either the aggregate stops being announced (if BGP requires a matching route), or it is still announced with nothing to absorb traffic for unused addresses in it: that traffic follows the upstream's default straight back to the upstream, a routing loop. Both are harmful.
